meta.title: 'Convert to ES6 module' generates invalid code when accessing '.default'
meta.fix_ref: microsoft/TypeScript#43309 (fix(services): convert to es6 module generate invalid code with default), a8ee22f73d, 2021-03-30; git tag --contains: first in v4.3-beta / v4.3.2
meta.build_notes: npm typescript@4.2.4 (2021-04-07) and typescript@4.3.2 (2021-05-26), both behind typescript-language-server@0.5.1 (the latest wrapper release before 4.3.2), started with the pinned tsserver.js; the reported TypeScript version is checked on every session. Wrapper 0.5.1 is installed with the dependencies of its release date (install_builds.wrapper_before). The wrapper logs no TypeScript version; the build check verifies that its tsserver child runs the pinned tsserver.js.
meta.notes: The CommonJS file suggestion TS80001 carries the 'Convert to ES module' fix in a .js file. The era wrapper returns quick fixes as bare commands (_typescript.applyWorkspaceEdit) without a code-action kind, so the edit spec selects by title only.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; no jsconfig.json, so tsserver uses an inferred project (node-fetch is not installed, which does not matter for the fix).

files.note: the file name is not given in the issue

repro.steps: Open index.js (require of node-fetch and a call of fetch.default()). Execute the 'Convert to ES module' quick fix. Reported: the result is "import { default } from 'node-fetch'; default()", which is invalid code; expected "import nodeFetch from 'node-fetch'; nodeFetch()". Probe: the fixed text must not have a parse error the original did not have.
